title: Stream-safe Retry Matrix & Idempotency Recipes for Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Leah Park
description: Background: Teams building on Redwood report inconsistent retry ergonomics between our language SDKs, especially around streaming chat and function-calling paths. Streaming SDKs today either (a) disable retries entirely, or (b) attempt naive reconnects that risk duplicated side effects. Goal: define a single cross-SDK recipe that (1) provides safe defaults for non-streaming and streaming endpoints, (2) defines a compact retry/backoff preset set, (3) standardizes idempotency key semantics and header names, and (4) supplies concrete language examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go.
scope: Produce design doc + API contract + SDK changes: (a) backoff presets (conservative/balanced/aggressive), (b) idempotency token semantics and header X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key, (c) per-endpoint retryability matrix (HTTP/GRPC codes + network errors), (d) stream resume protocol with resume tokens where safe, (e) tests and cross-sdk example snippets.
deliverables: design doc with matrix and presets
spec for idempotency header and token lifecycle
SDK defaults updated behind feature flag for 2 weeks
acceptance_criteria: Design reviewed and approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go)
Automated test coverage for retryable error cases >= 85% lines for retry code
Backoff presets implemented in all three SDKs and toggled by 'retry_preset' opt-in/out
Idempotency header is documented and accepted by API team; server supports idempotency token TTL and duplicate suppression metrics
decision_summary: We will ship opinionated SDK defaults but keep them opt-out for 2 release cycles: balanced preset enabled by default for idempotent non-streaming endpoints (generate/text/embeddings), and retries disabled for streaming endpoints by default. Streaming paths gain an opt-in 'resume' mode: if client supplies Resume-Token (opaque) + idempotency-key, the SDK will attempt a resumable reconnect on transient network failures. Rationale: most apps expect safe retries for synchronous calls; streaming semantics are more application-specific and risk side effects if retried automatically.
retry_presets:
Preset names and parameters (applied in SDKs):
- conservative: max_retries=2, base_delay=200ms, max_delay=2s, jitter=full, backoff=exponential, total_timeout=8s
- balanced: max_retries=4, base_delay=150ms, max_delay=3s, jitter=full, backoff=exponential, total_timeout=20s
- aggressive: max_retries=7, base_delay=100ms, max_delay=5s, jitter=full, backoff=exponential-with-cap, total_timeout=60s
Default mapping: non-streaming idempotent endpoints -> balanced; non-idempotent endpoints -> no SDK retry by default (require explicit enable); streaming endpoints -> retries OFF by default, resume-mode opt-in.
retryable_error_taxonomy: Retryable errors (SDKs should treat as transient by default): HTTP 429 (rate-limited), 502, 503, 504; gRPC UNAVAILABLE, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; network errors: ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, EPIPE, connection refused; TLS handshake failures where handshake timed out. Non-retryable: 400, 401, 403, 404, 422 (validation), 409 when conflict indicates change in state that is not safe to retry. For function-calling/tooling paths: treat any application-level error that indicates side-effect completion (200 with body error flag) as non-retryable. Special-case: 409 on idempotent endpoints may be considered retryable when server returns 'duplicate-detected' with idempotency-token echo; SDKs should surface server intent in structured error for client to decide.
idempotency_spec: Header: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key (string token). Semantics: token is opaque to server but returned in responses for diagnostics. Tokens are valid for 24 hours server-side; server deduplicates requests with same token+route+model-version. SDK behavior: generate UUIDv4 when user does not provide; allow user-supplied deterministic tokens (e.g., HMAC(namespace, payload) for semantic de-dup). SDKs should expose 'idempotency_key' parameter on request builders and should not mutate or re-use the same key across unrelated operations. Clear guidance: do NOT auto-generate idempotency keys for streaming sessions unless user explicitly requests resume-mode. When resume-mode is used, clients must pass both Resume-Token (server-provided) and X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key.
stream_resume_protocol: Resume-mode contract (opt-in): 1) Client starts a streaming session; server may periodically return a Resume-Token (opaque string) in 'meta' frames. 2) If client disconnects and re-connects within TTL, client supplies Resume-Token + same idempotency key to resume. 3) Server verifies that state matches (model version, prompt prefix). If mismatch, server returns UNRESUMABLE and client must restart full session. Safety: resume is allowed only for read-only tokenization/continuation streams and NOT allowed when the server indicates side effects (tool invocations) occurred unless server explicitly supports idempotent side-effect reconciliation. SDKs should provide 'resume_max_age' configuration and clear hooks: on_resume_success, on_resume_failure with provided reason.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Server-side dedupe increases storage/metrics costs (TTL for tokens).
- Aggressive SDK retries can increase tail load and amplify rate limits; mitigated via jitter and server-side backpressure signals.
- Resume-mode for streams introduces complexity and potential for resume mismatch; limit to opt-in and expose failure reasons clearly.
- Deterministic idempotency tokens (HMAC of immutable inputs) are powerful but may leak stable fingerprints if misused; document recommended HMAC/namespace pattern and warn about PII in token payloads.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + API): finalize matrix + header names + resume contract. Phase 2 (SDK changes behind feature flag): implement presets and idempotency param in Python/TS/Go with shared tests. Phase 3 (canary): enable balanced preset by default for non-stream endpoints for 2 weeks with telemetry. Phase 4: iterate on tweaks based on duplicate-detection metrics and errors surfaced by SDKs.
